title: Use of Variant Programs
raw_text:
9/29/26, 9:47 AM
Use of Variant Programs

When using variant programs for conditional billing, check whether the variants and their rates make sense from a technical and
application point of view. This applies particularly for complicated billing procedures such as backbilling or DPC, as well as for the

following points:

e Price block adjustment
e Use of TQUANT
e Physical values such as cosinus phi

e Consumption history
e (Previous) period consumption or demand

e Updating statistics

In the context menu (right click on an output operand), you can choose to display all of an output operand's schema steps that are
affected by the operand update in order to analyze the flow of data for operands in schema maintenance. This can be useful for
large and complicated schemas.

With conditional billing, you can also define new scenarios. When defining the conditional rates, you can use the following variant
programs:

e QUANT1A4X: Update for Quantity
e DEMANIA4X: Update for Demand

e COMPUI1X: Update for Amount

These variant programs generate info line items for individual TOU exceptions for a specific time.

For more information, see the system documentation for the variant programs.

Time-of-Use Exception Program

Use

You represent demand response programs in SAP IS-U as time-of-use exception programs. Events that occur during demand
response programs are referred to as time-of-use exceptions.

A time-of-use exception program (TOU exception program) groups time-of-use exceptions that belong to the same demand
response program. The participation of a customer in a TOU exception program is part of the contractual agreement between the
utilities company and the customer.

TOU exception programs represent the connection between conditional billing and the TOU exception.
